paragraphs.source_en: The significance of global hyperbolicity for singularity theorems stems from the following. Let U be globally hyperbolic and let p and q be points of U that can be joined by a timelike or null curve. Then there is a timelike or null geodesic between p and q which maximizes the length of timelike or null curves from p to q (fig. 1. 7). The method of proof is to show that the space of all timelike or null curves from p to q is compact in a certain topology. One then shows that the length of the curve is an upper semicontinuous function on this space. It must therefore attain its maximum, and the curve of maximum length will be a geodesic because otherwise a small variation will give a longer curve. One can now consider the second variation of the length of a geodesic y.
